slides.0.title: Côtes du Rhône and Villages Rules
slides.0.subtitle: Variety percentages and village names
slides.1.title: Côtes du Rhône: grape proportions
slides.1.highlights.0.title: The AOC and its wines
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The INAO specification cites the recognition and delimitation decree of 19 November 1937; red, rosé and white are allowed. About 26,800 ha in 2025 (Inter Rhône)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Main varieties for red and rosé
slides.1.highlights.1.content: The main varieties are Grenache, Syrah and Mourvèdre, together at least 70%; Grenache must be at least 30% (except for estates north of the Montélimar parallel)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Syrah + Mourvèdre
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Syrah and Mourvèdre together at least 20%; Caladoc, Couston and Marselan together at most 10%; white varieties in red wine at most 5%
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Measured on the whole estate
slides.1.highlights.3.content: The proportions apply to the estate's plantings (encépagement), not to the recipe of any single wine — the point most often misread in exams
slides.1.content: Côtes du Rhône is the valley-wide base appellation; its variety rules are tested on the estate's plantings, not on one bottle.
slides.2.title: Resolved: 20% or 15%?
slides.2.highlights.0.title: A phased introduction
slides.2.highlights.0.content: INAO text: 10% for new plantings from 2016; 20% for new plantings from 2019; and for vines already in production, 20% from the 2022 harvest. Until the 2023 harvest the national committee could lower it case by case
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Why sources differ
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Your 2021 Drive notes say 15%, a transitional version; WineWithSeth's 20% is the final one. The gap is about dates, not a contradiction
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Other figures (draft text)
slides.2.highlights.2.content: The 2026 draft modification states: yield 51 hl/ha (ceiling 60); minimum natural alcohol 11% in the south, 10.5% in the north. Draft wording — reference only, not tested
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Number of communes: open
slides.2.highlights.3.content: The INAO draft lists 176 communes in 7 départements (its own text says 6); WineWithSeth gives 172 communes in 6. The sources disagree, so the course says only "roughly 170-plus communes" and does not test it
slides.2.content: Check the date, then the version: the current minimum for Syrah + Mourvèdre (from the 2022 harvest) is 20%.
slides.3.title: Côtes du Rhône Villages
slides.3.highlights.0.title: The AOC and its area
slides.3.highlights.0.content: The INAO text cites a decree of 2 November 1966 (its history section says 1967); limited to four southern départements — Ardèche, Drôme, Gard and Vaucluse. Red, rosé and white are allowed
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Stricter proportions
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Red and rosé: main varieties (Grenache, Syrah, Mourvèdre) at least 80%; Grenache at least 40%; Syrah + Mourvèdre at least 25%. Your Drive note of 40% Grenache agrees
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Yields and alcohol (draft text)
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Draft text: Villages 44 hl/ha (ceiling 50), named villages 41 hl/ha (ceiling 45); minimum natural alcohol 12%, 12.5% for some named-village reds. Reference only, not tested
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Scale
slides.3.highlights.3.content: About 8,019 ha in 2025, of which about 5,285 ha carry a village name; red is about 96% of volume (Inter Rhône 2025)
slides.3.content: Villages is the layer between Côtes du Rhône and the crus: stricter proportions, southern départements only.
slides.4.title: The 21 named villages
slides.4.highlights.0.title: The 21 names (INAO)
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Chusclan, Gadagne, Massif d'Uchaux, Nyons, Plan de Dieu, Puyméras, Roaix, Rochegude, Rousset-les-Vignes, Sablet, Saint-Andéol, Saint-Gervais, Saint-Maurice, Saint-Pantaléon-les-Vignes, Sainte-Cécile, Séguret, Signargues, Suze-la-Rousse, Vaison-la-Romaine, Valréas, Visan
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Colour restrictions
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Chusclan may be red or rosé only; Gadagne, Massif d'Uchaux, Nyons, Plan de Dieu, Puyméras, Saint-Andéol, Sainte-Cécile, Signargues, Suze-la-Rousse and Vaison-la-Romaine may be red or white only (no rosé); the other 10 may be red, rosé or white
slides.4.highlights.2.title: The path up to cru
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Several of today's crus began as place names under Côtes du Rhône or Villages: Gigondas (1971), Vacqueyras (1990), Beaumes-de-Venise (2005), Vinsobres (2006), Cairanne (2016), Laudun (2024)
slides.4.highlights.3.title: Reading the label
slides.4.highlights.3.content: "Côtes du Rhône Villages + village" is still the Villages AOC; a cru is a stand-alone AOC and no longer carries the Villages wording
slides.4.content: The colour restrictions are good exam material, but you need only remember the Chusclan exception and the pattern.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
In the Côtes du Rhône rules for red wine, what is the minimum for Grenache (measured on the estate's plantings)?
At least 30% (estates north of the Montélimar parallel excepted). 40% is the Villages requirement.
From which harvest must vines already in production meet the 20% minimum for Syrah + Mourvèdre combined?
New plantings: 10% from 2016, 20% from 2019; vines in production from the 2022 harvest. The 15% in older notes is a transitional version.
What is the minimum for Grenache in red Côtes du Rhône Villages?
Villages requires at least 40% Grenache and 25% Syrah + Mourvèdre — stricter than Côtes du Rhône.
How many villages may add their name after Côtes du Rhône Villages?
21 (INAO specification and Inter Rhône agree). 18 is the number of crus — do not confuse them.
